--help.before: Print help and exit 0. Typer exposes --help only. Direct argparse also accepts -h.
--help.problem: Help and aliases differ by entry parser. Root help mixes the command list with a long usage guide.
--help.after: Support -h and --help everywhere. Keep root help short and command help specific. Generate help from one option declaration.
--help.acceptance: Every command/action has accurate defaults, units and one working example.

--version.before: Root-only boolean. Prints sxr version and exits 0 when the root callback runs.
--version.problem: Unavailable after a command. A package version alone does not identify an uncommitted source build.
--version.after: Keep root --version. Document its placement. Optionally include build revision in a separate machine-readable version result.
--version.compatibility: No change to current version output in this pass.
--version.acceptance: Root --version exits 0 without reading transcripts or starting a worker.

--codex.before: Restricts session discovery to Codex. Mutually exclusive with --claude. Inherited root/command flags are OR-merged.
--codex.problem: Provider selection is ignored before non-session commands. Combined flags at different levels can conflict.
--codex.after: Retain the switch and mutual exclusion. Reject it where irrelevant. State the provider on every scope-bearing command.
--codex.compatibility: Do not change existing provider defaults in this review's first implementation pass.
--codex.acceptance: Root/local placement selects the same provider and conflicts have the same error.

--claude.before: Selects Claude. This is already the default for most session views, but find defaults to both providers.
--claude.problem: Shared Typer help incorrectly calls Claude the default even for find.
--claude.after: Retain the switch. Give find its correct Only Claude wording and make each command's default scope visible.
--claude.compatibility: Help correction only for existing valid uses.
--claude.acceptance: Both find help paths say both providers by default and Only Claude for this flag.

--path.before: Selects recorded project cwd, resolving relative paths, ~ and symlinks. Defaults to actual process cwd. Command value overrides root value.
--path.problem: Path has a different meaning from --file and is silently ignored by some root-prefixed commands.
--path.after: Retain project matching semantics. Describe recorded cwd explicitly. Reject unsupported placement rather than ignoring it.
--path.compatibility: Retain exact matching by default and existing symlink normalization.
--path.acceptance: Relative, home-expanded and physical paths select the same recorded project.

--file.before: Reads one verified JSONL transcript, detects provider and validates explicit provider/project/profile constraints. Avoids rediscovery.
--file.problem: Its exact-file behavior is not reflected consistently in every command's follow-up. Some irrelevant root uses are ignored.
--file.after: Keep --file as the stable exact-source selection. Preserve it in every generated follow-up and reject conflicting selectors.
--file.compatibility: Do not broaden explicit files into children or duplicate copies.
--file.acceptance: All relevant commands read only the named file and reject provider/path conflicts.

--recursive.before: Includes descendant recorded project directories in addition to the selected exact cwd.
--recursive.problem: A positive-only toggle cannot disable an inherited true value. It is ineffective with some all-project/file combinations.
--recursive.after: Retain descendant matching. Document valid combinations and reject irrelevant scope modifiers. Keep child transcripts distinct from descendant project directories.
--recursive.compatibility: Preserve path matching boundaries so /repo-other is not a descendant.

--worktrees.before: Adds registered Git worktree paths for the selected repository. Combines with --recursive.
--worktrees.problem: It can be accepted where --all-projects or an unrelated command makes it ineffective.
--worktrees.after: Retain registered worktree discovery. Make no-repository behavior and irrelevant combinations explicit.
--worktrees.acceptance: Main repo and linked worktree yield matching declared scope without sibling-directory guessing.

--claude-root.before: Repeatable Claude config root. Explicit roots replace CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/default ~/.claude. Root and command occurrences accumulate.
--claude-root.problem: Cannot be used with --codex, including when the inherited flag was added elsewhere.
--claude-root.after: Retain repeatable roots and provider validation. Show which profiles are included and preserve them in follow-ups.
--claude-root.compatibility: Keep root/command accumulation and physical-path deduplication.
--claude-root.acceptance: Both profiles are searched exactly once and copied follow-ups preserve their scope.

--include-agents.before: Includes nested Claude transcripts in ordinary views. find already includes children, so the flag is redundant there. It is rejected with --codex.
--include-agents.problem: Same flag is a scope change in one command and a no-op in another. find has no exclusion counterpart.
--include-agents.after: Keep inclusion alias and add --no-agents to find. Document current per-command defaults. Validate provider-specific flags consistently.
--include-agents.compatibility: Add exclusion without changing default discovery. Preserve --include-agents for scripts.
--include-agents.acceptance: The default, explicit inclusion and explicit exclusion have clear fixture-backed membership.

--archives.before: Adds Codex archived_sessions in ordinary Codex views. find includes the archive root when present; explicit flag also makes an absent archive root part of coverage.
--archives.problem: find lacks an exclusion counterpart. Shared help conceals its broader default.
--archives.after: Keep inclusion and add --no-archives to find. Explain present-root discovery versus explicit missing-root coverage.
--archives.compatibility: Do not remove the existing --archives spelling or alter missing-root completeness silently.
--archives.acceptance: Active/archive fixtures and a missing explicitly requested root produce documented membership and coverage.

--coverage.before: Reports discovered roots/sources on stderr. Ordinary discovery also reports coverage for no sessions or multiple roots. find JSON includes coverage regardless of this flag.
--coverage.problem: Coverage completeness semantics differ between read views and find. Displayed coverage need not imply a complete search.
--coverage.after: Keep stderr diagnostics and structured find coverage. Label unavailable roots and distinguish discovery counts from searched source counts.
--coverage.compatibility: Keep machine-readable stdout free from notices.
--coverage.acceptance: Missing roots remain visible and no text notice breaks JSON stdout.

--since.before: Keeps sessions whose start is on/after a date, ISO instant, today (UTC midnight), or @N start. Filters sessions, not events. Root scope is inherited.
--since.problem: Some session commands accept this only before the command. Handles are renumbered after filtering. Invalid/missing starts are excluded.
--since.after: Expose the same flag after every session command. Keep inclusive start-time semantics and explicitly document UTC and handle resolution.
--since.compatibility: Add missing placements. Do not reinterpret this as an event timestamp or last-activity filter.
--since.acceptance: Before/after-command forms select identical sessions, including timezone-offset cases.

--before.before: Keeps sessions started strictly before the bound. Dates/today mean UTC midnight. Bounds using handles are resolved before narrowing the scope.
--before.problem: Only root placement works on several views. Old sessions resumed today remain in --before today despite live-session hints.
--before.after: Expose the same flag after every session command and remove claims that it always excludes live/current sessions.
--before.acceptance: A resumed old session is retained, while a session started today is excluded. Both flag placements agree.

show --around.before: Selects every event whose physical sequence lies within N plus/minus --context. Whole text. Integer has no minimum.
show --around.problem: Zero/negative coordinates are accepted. --type silently overrides --around.
show --around.after: Require a positive physical record coordinate. Intersect with --type. Reject combination with --range.
show --around.compatibility: Invalid windows become usage errors instead of empty success/selection.
show --around.acceptance: Negative/zero coordinates exit 2; the type-filtered window selects the expected source records.

show --context.before: Half-width for --around, default 10 physical sequence positions. Ignored without --around.
show --context.problem: Negative values are accepted and can make a window empty.
show --context.after: Require a nonnegative half-width and require --around when explicitly supplied.
show --context.compatibility: Reject meaningless combinations that were previously ignored.
show --context.acceptance: --context 0 selects the center record and -1 exits 2.

show --range.before: Selects inclusive physical record coordinates A:B. Also accepts A-B. Reversed ranges return empty. It is overridden by --type or --around.
show --range.problem: Invalid, reversed and conflicting selections are not handled consistently.
show --range.after: Validate positive bounds with start <= end. Intersect a range with --type and reject simultaneous --around.
show --range.compatibility: Reversed ranges become usage errors. Keep A-B as an alias.
show --range.acceptance: Invalid/reversed bounds exit 2; valid boundaries include both endpoints.

show --type.before: Matches normalized event kind exactly or as a dot prefix. It takes precedence over all other base selectors and prints whole text.
show --type.problem: Help says record type, which can be confused with raw provider type. Typos simply return empty.
show --type.after: Name this normalized event kind in help, list known kinds and compose with time/sequence windows. Retain prefix matching for forward-compatible kinds.
show --type.compatibility: Combining existing flags will narrow the window rather than ignoring it.
show --type.acceptance: Documented kinds match fixture events and unknown kinds get an informative empty-result notice.

show --tail.before: Last N selected events, whole text. Zero means none and exits 1. Negative values fail. Applied after base selection.
show --tail.problem: With --json, N counts normalized events before physical-record deduplication, so one multi-event source line can give surprising counts.
show --tail.after: Keep zero/negative behavior. State the unit explicitly and make JSON selection limits count complete distinct source records.
show --tail.compatibility: Preserve text event behavior unless a versioned source-record unit is adopted across show.
show --tail.acceptance: Tail boundaries and multi-block physical records are tested separately in text/raw JSON.

show --thinking.before: Adds thinking events to the default skeleton. Ignored when --errors, --type or other zoom selection replaces the skeleton.
show --thinking.problem: No option help explains what is added or when it is ignored.
show --thinking.after: Retain inclusion but document combination rules and avoid silent overrides under the shared selection pipeline.
show --thinking.acceptance: The flag adds the expected kinds and combination behavior is shown in help.

show --tools.before: Adds tool result events. Tool call events already appear by default.
show --tools.problem: The name suggests all tools, not specifically their results. Help has no explanation.
show --tools.after: Add --tool-results as the primary name and keep --tools as a compatibility alias.
show --tools.compatibility: Alias addition, no removal in the first migration.
show --tools.acceptance: Both spellings include the same result events.

show --errors.before: Selects is_error or err-tagged events only when --full or a zoom/type branch has not taken precedence.
show --errors.problem: --full --errors includes non-error records. Different selectors silently override this filter.
show --errors.after: Apply error filtering within the selected window/full set. Explain inclusion of failed calls as well as error results.
show --errors.acceptance: Every emitted event satisfies the error predicate and full text is preserved.

show --full.before: Includes all event kinds and disables text trimming. Earlier type/around/range selection still wins. --full wins over --errors in skeleton selection.
show --full.problem: Combines record selection and display completeness, and disables the error filter unexpectedly.
show --full.after: Retain full all-kind/whole-text behavior when used alone. Make explicit filters constrain it and document that --limit still applies.
show --full.compatibility: Standalone --full remains compatible. Combined filter behavior changes.
show --full.acceptance: Standalone full emits all events. Full plus errors emits only complete error events.

show --budget.before: 40000-character threshold by default, overridden by SXR_BUDGET. Crossing it switches to line trimming rather than enforcing a hard output maximum. Zero/negative disables. JSON, full and zooms bypass it.
show --budget.problem: The name looks like a strict budget. Negatives silently behave as unlimited.
show --budget.after: Describe it as a compact-display threshold, reject negatives and retain 0 as the explicit disabled value. State when full/zoom/JSON bypass it.
show --budget.compatibility: Keep existing positive threshold behavior and unlimited 0.
show --budget.acceptance: Positive budgets trigger documented trimming; negative input is a usage error.

show --line-limit.before: Per-line cap while trimming, default SXR_LINE_LIMIT or 200. Zero/negative disables most line caps. Tool result middle trimming still uses fixed 200+120.
show --line-limit.problem: It is not a consistent cap across event kinds and has no minimum validation.
show --line-limit.after: Reject negatives, define 0 as no per-line trim and apply the same explicit cap policy to all displayed event kinds.
show --line-limit.compatibility: May change compact result summaries. Preserve access to whole text.
show --line-limit.acceptance: Every event kind follows the selected cap, including tool results.

prompts --all.before: Disables the human provenance predicate and includes every user-role event, including injected instructions and tool results. Does not lift explicit row/budget limits.
prompts --all.problem: Users read all as all human prompts. It changes the meaning of the command.
prompts --all.after: Make --all remove row and text presentation limits while retaining human selection. Move current selection expansion to --include-context.
prompts --all.compatibility: Breaking semantic change. Announce migration of old --all users to --include-context.
prompts --all.acceptance: --all excludes injected/tool records even with -n 1 and --budget 1 supplied.

prompts --budget.before: Uses explicit value, else SXR_BUDGET, else 40000 to decide whether prompt text is trimmed. Zero/negative disables.
prompts --budget.problem: Whole human input requires knowing --budget 0 and can be affected by environment settings.
prompts --budget.after: Default prompts to whole text independent of an implicit environment budget. Retain an explicitly supplied nonnegative budget as an opt-in compact threshold.
prompts --budget.compatibility: Default output can be larger. Preserve explicit positive budgets and 0.
prompts --budget.acceptance: A long human prompt is verbatim by default under SXR_BUDGET=1.

prompts --line-limit.before: Caps prompt lines only after the budget activates trimming. Default SXR_LINE_LIMIT or 200. Zero/negative removes the cap.
prompts --line-limit.problem: It does not itself request a compact view and accepts negative input.
prompts --line-limit.after: Keep as an advanced compact-view control, reject negatives, and ensure it cannot silently truncate the default complete prompt view.
prompts --line-limit.acceptance: No line limit applies in the plain default view; explicit compact output obeys the cap.

grep --count.before: Ranks sessions by number of matching normalized events, with first matching sequence. Output becomes per-session aggregates. Not physical occurrences or shell grep line counts.
grep --count.problem: The short -c resembles line/occurrence counts. It overrides -l, context and budget without validation.
grep --count.after: Keep event-count semantics and explain the unit. Reject incompatible output-mode flags and make ignored display flags explicit.
grep --count.compatibility: Preserve counts so existing retrieval decisions stay comparable.
grep --count.acceptance: Multiple hits in one event count once; multiple events in one record remain clearly documented.

grep --fixed.before: Escapes the pattern as a literal substring. Smart-case still applies unless -i is set.
grep --fixed.problem: Some users expect literal to imply case-sensitive. Current help does not make their independence prominent.
grep --fixed.after: Retain behavior and document case handling beside literal matching.
grep --fixed.acceptance: Literal punctuation and explicit ignore-case produce expected results.

grep --context.before: Prints N neighboring normalized events per match. Windows may overlap and repeat. --limit counts match windows. Negative N behaves like no context.
grep --context.problem: Not physical-line context despite familiar grep spelling. JSON/-c/-l ignore context.
grep --context.after: Require nonnegative N. Document event/window units, merge overlapping windows, and reject incompatible output modes.
grep --context.compatibility: Merged windows reduce duplicates in text. Preserve hit identity and order.
grep --context.acceptance: Overlapping hits do not duplicate context unexpectedly. Invalid combinations fail clearly.

grep --ignore-case.before: Forces case-insensitive matching. Otherwise lowercase patterns ignore case and any capital makes matching case-sensitive.
grep --ignore-case.problem: No material defect in this switch.
grep --ignore-case.after: Retain -i/--ignore-case and explain its interaction with -F in command help.
grep --ignore-case.acceptance: Lowercase, capitalized and -i fixture queries have the advertised matching behavior.

grep --files-with-matches.before: Prints matching session short IDs, not file paths. Takes precedence over JSON and context unless -c selected the count path.
grep --files-with-matches.problem: The long name promises files. Combined --json output is not JSON.
grep --files-with-matches.after: Add --ids as the clear primary alias. Keep -l/--files-with-matches for compatibility. Emit structured session identity when JSON is requested.
grep --files-with-matches.compatibility: Existing plain ID output stays available. JSON combination changes from invalid to valid.
grep --files-with-matches.acceptance: Every JSON line parses and contains full ID/provider/path. No ambiguity from short-ID collisions.

grep --regexp.before: Provides one pattern, including a leading dash. A single positional then becomes the session selector. Additional positionals fail.
grep --regexp.problem: Familiar grep -e often accepts repeated patterns, but this option accepts one.
grep --regexp.after: Retain one-pattern behavior and document it. Preserve the leading-dash escape hatch and targeted positional error.
grep --regexp.compatibility: Do not silently combine repeated patterns without a separately reviewed syntax.
grep --regexp.acceptance: A dash-leading literal/regex and session argument are unambiguous.

grep --all.before: Only affects -c by retaining zero-match session rows, but if every session has zero matches the command returns empty and prints none. Has no effect in normal grep.
grep --all.problem: All has a different meaning from prompts and from unlimited output. The all-zero case contradicts inclusion.
grep --all.after: Add --include-zero for count-table selection. Redefine --all as uncapped complete output and make the all-zero count table printable with --include-zero.
grep --all.compatibility: Breaking --all semantics need migration notes. Preserve zero-match exit 1 even when reporting zero rows as data.
grep --all.acceptance: --include-zero includes every scoped session, including when all counts are zero.

grep --sort.before: String accepted then validated as matches or started. Controls only -c. started sorts timestamp strings oldest first.
grep --sort.problem: Accepted on normal grep with no effect. Offset timestamps can sort incorrectly.
grep --sort.after: Restrict to count mode, declare choices in parser and sort normalized UTC instants for started.
grep --sort.compatibility: Corrected ordering can change rank but not counts.
grep --sort.acceptance: Invalid choices or use outside count mode fail. Offset timestamps sort by actual start.

grep --after-context.before: Hidden -A/--after-context is parsed then always rejected with a symmetric -C hint.
grep --after-context.problem: Common grep syntax is recognized only to produce an error.
grep --after-context.after: Support nonnegative asymmetric context, or retain the targeted error until implemented. Proposed end state supports -A with -B and clear -C conflict validation.
grep --after-context.compatibility: Additive capability. Keep current recovery hint until support ships.
grep --after-context.acceptance: Only following context appears for -A; ambiguous -A/-B/-C combinations fail.

grep --before-context.before: Hidden -B/--before-context is parsed then always rejected with a symmetric -C hint.
grep --before-context.problem: A familiar flag exists in the parser but cannot perform its advertised conventional task.
grep --before-context.after: Support nonnegative preceding context with the same combination rules as -A.
grep --before-context.compatibility: Additive capability after a scoped implementation.
grep --before-context.acceptance: Only preceding context appears for -B; negative counts fail.

grep --budget.before: Limits printed match blocks by total character size, default SXR_BUDGET or 40000. Always permits the first block. -n 0 and JSON disable it. -c ignores it.
grep --budget.problem: The same name as show/prompts means output stopping instead of display trimming. -n changes two separate controls.
grep --budget.after: Keep a documented search-output budget with omission metadata. Make -n count only results. --all disables row, character and per-match caps.
grep --budget.compatibility: -n 0 no longer silently changes an explicit budget. Provide --all as the direct migration.
grep --budget.acceptance: Budget never splits a logical result. Omitted results are visible in text and structured metadata.

cmds --grep.before: Smart-case regex over full command text/tool summaries. Nonempty filter with no selector changes scope from newest to all sessions. Empty string behaves as no filter.
cmds --grep.problem: A filter unexpectedly broadens selection. Literal matching requires manually escaping regex.
cmds --grep.after: Keep regex matching but make scope independent through --all-sessions. Add -F/--fixed for literal recorded-command search.
cmds --grep.compatibility: Migrate current implicit all-scope searches. Keep pattern matching over full stored command text.
cmds --grep.acceptance: Filter changes only matching rows, not sessions. Literal punctuation can be searched directly.

find --all-projects.before: Searches every project in selected provider stores, bypassing cwd/path filtering. Time/provider/exclusions still apply.
find --all-projects.problem: Can be combined with --path/--recursive/--worktrees whose intended effect becomes unclear or is ignored.
find --all-projects.after: Retain explicit broad scope and reject incompatible project modifiers.
find --all-projects.compatibility: Previously redundant combinations become targeted usage errors.
find --all-projects.acceptance: Unrelated projects are included only through explicit all-project scope.

find --any.before: Uses OR across clues instead of requiring every clue somewhere in a session. Quoted phrase clues remain grouped.
find --any.problem: No material defect in the flag.
find --any.after: Retain behavior and explain all-clues default beside it.
find --any.acceptance: AND/OR and phrase fixtures produce expected result sets.

find --index.before: Without a query prepares ranked FTS/catalog data and exits 0 even with zero results. With a query performs a normal search and also makes an empty result exit 0.
find --index.problem: An operational flag changes no-hit search exit behavior. Differs from sxr index preparation.
find --index.after: Define this as preparation-only when no query is given. With a query, preserve ordinary search exit semantics or reject the combination explicitly. Share preparation with index.
find --index.compatibility: Scripts using query plus --index need a migration note.
find --index.acceptance: Query no-hit remains exit 1 regardless of index preparation. Preparation-only success is exit 0.

find --paths.before: Returns matching source paths without ranking/excerpts. Default limit changes from 5 to all. --json returns a paths envelope with coverage.
find --paths.problem: Mode-specific default is easy to miss, but useful for pipelines.
find --paths.after: Keep all-path default and exact path projection. State limit unit and compatibility with --json in help.
find --paths.compatibility: Preserve the current structured paths envelope.
find --paths.acceptance: Text and JSON contain the same paths with the same explicit -n cap.

find --include-current.before: Disables automatic exclusion of the invoking Codex ID from CODEX_THREAD_ID or CODEX_SESSION_ID. --file already disables automatic exclusion.
find --include-current.problem: Name sounds provider-neutral but automatic exclusion is Codex-only. Explicit --exclude-session still wins.
find --include-current.after: Retain behavior. Describe environment-based Codex detection and precedence clearly.
find --include-current.compatibility: Do not introduce heuristic current-session guessing.
find --include-current.acceptance: Known current Codex session is included, unless also explicitly excluded. Exact --file works as documented.

find --exclude-session.before: Repeatable full-ID exclusion, exact and case-sensitive. Does not resolve @N or prefixes. Coverage records excluded counts.
find --exclude-session.problem: Session argument forms accepted elsewhere do not work here and a typo can silently exclude nothing.
find --exclude-session.after: Retain stable full-ID exclusion and document it. Report unmatched explicit exclusions in diagnostics without accidentally broadening search.
find --exclude-session.compatibility: Avoid rejecting valid exclusions outside the currently narrowed scope without explanation.
find --exclude-session.acceptance: Full IDs are excluded, prefixes are not guessed and unmatched values are visible.

skills --index.before: Forces discovery and hashing. With --root remembers new default roots. With no query, table rows are suppressed and only a discovery summary is printed.
skills --index.problem: It combines cache refresh and persistent discovery-scope configuration.
skills --index.after: Retain explicit refresh. Describe root persistence and print resolved roots before/with the completion summary.
skills --index.compatibility: Do not change default roots through ordinary lookup.
skills --index.acceptance: A scoped --index updates the saved root selection and the following lookup uses it.

skills --root.before: Repeatable discovery root. With --index replaces remembered default roots. Without --index uses a separate transient scoped map.
skills --root.problem: Same flag has persistent and temporary effects depending on --index.
skills --root.after: Keep both uses but explain the distinction directly in flag help and structured metadata.
skills --root.compatibility: Preserve separate map keys and no accidental default-map mutation.
skills --root.acceptance: Transient lookups leave remembered roots unchanged; explicit indexing updates them.

skills --defaults.before: Requires --index and cannot combine with --root. Restores HOME plus configured external profile roots.
skills --defaults.problem: The name does not reveal that it resets remembered discovery roots.
skills --defaults.after: Add --reset-roots as the clearer primary alias and retain --defaults.
skills --defaults.acceptance: Reset restores the documented root set without removing unrelated cache files.

skills --paths.before: Prints canonical SKILL.md paths, one per content group by default, with unlimited groups unless -n given. --json instead prints the full skills envelope.
skills --paths.problem: Combined flags do not project the same paths in JSON. A content group can hide other installed copies.
skills --paths.after: Keep text behavior. Make --paths --json project the same path list, with explicit copy/alias controls.
skills --paths.compatibility: Path-only JSON is a schema change. Preserve ordinary --json groups.
skills --paths.acceptance: JSON paths equal text paths under the same copy/alias/limit settings.

skills --aliases.before: Requires --paths. Adds symlink aliases from selected records. It can print more lines than -n because the limit applies before alias expansion.
skills --aliases.problem: -n looks like a path cap but actually caps groups/files before expansion.
skills --aliases.after: Document the selected-result unit or cap final emitted paths in path mode. Proposed path mode applies limits after deduplication/alias expansion.
skills --aliases.compatibility: The selected path subset may change under a cap.
skills --aliases.acceptance: No more than N distinct paths are emitted and JSON/text agree.

skills --copies.before: Shows every matching physical file instead of grouping identical content hashes. Does not itself request symlink aliases.
skills --copies.problem: Copy files and aliases are easily conflated.
skills --copies.after: Retain independent content-copy and symlink controls, with one compact example explaining both.
skills --copies.acceptance: Identical contents at two physical paths and one symlink produce the expected distinct locations.

skills --exact.before: Matches the whole skill directory name or an alias directory name, case-insensitively. Requires a nonempty query.
skills --exact.problem: Exact applies to directory names, not full path bytes or SKILL.md content.
skills --exact.after: Retain behavior and clarify the matched field.
skills --exact.acceptance: Whole directory names match and substring-only clues do not.

skills --clear.before: Removes default skills.json and remembered roots. Rejects query, root, index and defaults, but accepts several irrelevant output/filter flags. Transient root maps remain.
skills --clear.problem: Clear sounds like all skill caches, yet only the default map is removed. Ignored combinations hide mistakes.
skills --clear.after: State the exact cleared extent and reject all meaningless combinations. Keep scoped-map removal as a separate explicit future operation if needed.
skills --clear.compatibility: Preserve existing default-map-only scope in the first pass.
skills --clear.acceptance: Default map is removed, transient maps remain, and help states this precisely.

index --clear.before: Removes the whole shared search.sqlite3 database and journal/WAL files if present. Early branch ignores scope/provider flags. Does not remove skill maps or salt.
index --clear.problem: Scope flags look like they might constrain clearing but do not.
index --clear.after: Keep explicit whole-session-cache clearing and reject scope/limit combinations. Report exact cache kinds removed and retained.
index --clear.compatibility: No transcript files are affected. Previously ignored scope flags become errors.
index --clear.acceptance: Cache clear extent matches documentation, including an absent database case.

init --write.before: Writes/replaces the marked primer block in the selected target. Mutually exclusive with --check. Bare init is print-only.
init --write.problem: Target inference can reach a parent AGENTS.md, which should be visible to the caller.
init --write.after: Keep explicit writing and idempotence. Report the resolved target and preserve all text outside the block.
init --write.compatibility: No broader write authorization or target search introduced.
init --write.acceptance: Repeated writes are unchanged and unrelated target text survives exactly.

init --check.before: Exits 0 when a block exists with the current version tag, even if its body was edited. Missing/outdated is 1, invalid markers or IO failure is 2.
init --check.problem: Version equality is not content equality.
init --check.after: Compare the generated primer block's content as well as its version, while ignoring unrelated outside text.
init --check.compatibility: Stricter checks may reveal manually altered blocks.
init --check.acceptance: Changed current-version content returns 1 with an update explanation.

init --global.before: Requires --write or --check and cannot combine with FILE. Chooses ~/.agents/AGENTS.md, else ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, else ~/AGENTS.md.
init --global.problem: Does not use CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex/AGENTS.md. The target name is not obvious from global.
init --global.after: Document the exact fallback chain and resolved destination. Keep selection unchanged until a separate profile-target decision.
init --global.compatibility: No automatic change to existing instruction files.
init --global.acceptance: The reported path matches the documented fallback under synthetic home directories.

secrets --candidates.before: Adds entropy-tier candidates to the certain/probable masked worklist. Propagates through the group to audit. Accepted before clean but ignored by clean.
secrets --candidates.problem: Audit-only selection is accepted with a rewriting action where it has no effect.
secrets --candidates.after: Keep candidates audit-only. Reject it when clean is selected and state that clean never rewrites entropy candidates.
secrets --candidates.compatibility: Invalid clean combinations become explicit usage errors.
secrets --candidates.acceptance: Candidates appear in audit only and never reach preview/apply rewriting.

secrets audit --candidates.before: Includes noisy entropy candidates in the masked audit; combines with parent candidate flag using OR.
secrets audit --candidates.problem: Parent and child flag placement is implicit.
secrets audit --candidates.after: Keep inheritance within audit and show this option on the documented audit action.
secrets audit --candidates.acceptance: Parent/local audit placement yields the same masked worklist.

secrets clean --apply.before: Writes all selected certain/probable replacements atomically, skips live/changed files and clears session caches before/after. -n limits output only. No backup is retained.
secrets clean --apply.problem: The default preview's printed apply command drops provider/path/session/date/file selection.
secrets clean --apply.after: Keep explicit --apply. Print a correctly quoted exact follow-up preserving selection, including --file. Expose applied/skipped/failed totals.
secrets clean --apply.compatibility: Retain atomic validation and current authorization boundary. Do not expand the write scope.
secrets clean --apply.acceptance: Preview follow-up selects exactly the previewed physical files. A report cap never limits validation or rewriting.

serve --foreground.before: Hidden PATH argument selects a socket and starts a foreground worker instead of running status/stop. Available only through direct argparse.
serve --foreground.problem: Overrides action and has different parser availability depending on root flags.
serve --foreground.after: Keep private launcher compatibility and validate it only in a dedicated internal launch mode with consistent parsing.
serve --foreground.compatibility: Native launcher contract must remain supported.
serve --foreground.acceptance: Invalid action/foreground combinations fail before starting a listener.

serve --idle.before: Hidden float, default 300. Used only with --foreground. Values <=0 fail; NaN/Infinity pass that check. Otherwise ignored.
serve --idle.problem: Non-finite and irrelevant values can pass parsing. Typer wrapper rejects the flag.
serve --idle.after: Require a finite positive timeout in foreground mode and reject the option in status/stop mode. Share parsing.
serve --idle.acceptance: 0, negative, NaN and Infinity fail before any worker side effect.
